correctness.rationale: All rates, dimensions, quantifiers and equality cases are explicit. Gamma Laplace transforms yield C_k. SymPy rederives three positive H rational functions and strictly negative logarithmic curvatures, establishing one crossing for each pair. At t12, the exact positive-remainder polynomial identity forces t23<t12; continuity and uniqueness force t13 between them. The cubic root monotonicity and asymptotic endpoints are proved analytically. The supplied checker passed 438 assertions, which are supplementary to the proof.

originality.rationale: The established gamma Laplace and consecutive-reaction formulas are credited, not claimed. The inspected hydrology and reactor design sources did not imply the full all-positive-rate strict ordering of the three pairwise switching times; the result rules out extra crossings and gives a nontrivial all-parameter exact order. The closest local previously published comparisons concern density windows, not dual-rate transformed responses. This is a best-knowledge, provisional priority finding, not an assertion of worldwide uniqueness.
residual_risks: Broad classical chemical-reactor literature on series first-order reactions and stirred-tank trains may contain an equivalent global stage-count ordering; this was not exhaustively ruled out.
Source inspection covers accessible primary materials and selected scholarly searches, not all older theses or books.
The mathematical model itself is a deliberately idealized dual-exponential transit-time response.

value.rationale: At fixed mean, reduced travel-time variance does not impose a monotone ranking on the two-rate response. The complete three-model phase diagram identifies a previously unproven sharp restriction: a genuine intermediate shape-2 optimum and three separately ordered pairwise crossovers for all positive kinetic contrasts. The scalar setup is a transparent benchmark for reactive-water-transit and consecutive-reaction cascade interpretations; this structural classification, rather than mere computation of Laplace transforms, provides the contribution.
